content:
As the WhatsApp username feature prepares to officially launch, the app now allows users to record usernames, names, and phone numbers when saving contacts. Details below.

New contact feature adds a username field, rolling out gradually to some WhatsApp users

While the username feature has long been a standard offering on most messaging platforms, WhatsApp has only recently begun moving away from relying solely on phone numbers to identify users.

WhatsApp previously began rolling out a username reservation system, allowing users to register their preferred usernames ahead of the feature's official launch to prevent scammers from impersonating identities.

WhatsApp began enabling the username feature for some iPhone users several weeks ago.

According to WABetaInfo, WhatsApp has now added a username field when users add new contacts, located between the last name field and the phone number field.

Source: WABetaInfo

WABetaInfo points out that the username field appears to be gradually rolling out to some users on both the WhatsApp beta and stable versions.

When testing with the latest stable version, the author found that although the field is now displayed, the system still shows a message saying "this username is not on WhatsApp" even when the entered username does exist.

Nonetheless, this marks another step forward for WhatsApp in gradually catching up with its competitors, adding a basic feature that many consider long overdue.
